title: 🐛 Pagination doesn't get the correct page when use routing after relodad
body:
### 🐛 Current behavior

After navigate with the pagination, for example to the page 2, and reload the page the pagination will show the page 1  instead of page 2 that is the truly page that is requested (when use routing with Next)

### 🔍 Steps to reproduce

1. In the index click in "[Go to the brand Samsung](https://hnivvj-3000.csb.app/brands/samsung)"
2. Click in the page 2 https://hnivvj-3000.csb.app/brands/samsung?instant_search%5Bpage%5D=2
3. Refresh the page
4. You will see the page 1 as active but the URL show the page two as active

### Live reproduction

https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/algolia-next-static-get-server-state-bug-hnivvj

### 💭 Expected behavior

When a url contains the active page, this is the one that should be displayed

### Package version

eact-instantsearch-hooks-web: 6.41.0

### Operating system

macOS 13.3.1

### Browser

Firefox 112.0.2

Hello @RodrigoTomeES!

Server side rendering on Next.js using [`createInstantSearchRouterNext()`](https://www.algolia.com/doc/api-reference/widgets/instantsearch-next-router/react-hooks/#widget-param-routeroptions) is not supported with [`getStaticProps()`](https://nextjs.org/docs/api-reference/data-fetching/get-static-props).
In static mode, you can't retrieve the query parameters because pages are generated at build time, thus the `serverUrl` is not correct.

You can use `getServerSideProps()` instead as shown here: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch/blob/master/examples/react-hooks/next/pages/index.tsx#L85-L99

Hope that's clear!

Hi @RodrigoTomeES,

Thanks for your message. It's great to hear that you've been able to use the `createInstanceSearchRoute()` function with filters even without SSR. However, I wanted to clarify that our routing system is based on query parameters, and `getStaticProps()` doesn't provide query parameters out of the box (https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/17269). While it may be possible to work around this limitation in custom ways, we don't officially support such approaches. I updated our documentation to clarify the support of `getStaticProps()`.

If you have any further questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to reach out.
